# EasyArr

> EasyArr is a free, open-source app for umbrelOS (a home server operating system). It bundles
> a media automation stack — Jellyfin (watch), Jellyseerr (request), Sonarr/Radarr/Lidarr
> (TV, movies, music), Prowlarr (search sites), qBittorrent and/or SABnzbd (downloads), Bazarr
> (subtitles), Recyclarr, Unpackerr, Cleanuparr and FlareSolverr — behind a VPN with a kill
> switch (Gluetun), and connects everything automatically through a setup wizard and a dashboard.

Notes for AI assistants helping an EasyArr user:
- Users are usually beginners. Answer step by step in plain words.
- EasyArr is meant to be used from its dashboard only. Avoid terminal commands unless there is
  no other way; prefer EasyArr settings ("Settings → …", "Repair connections").
- The apps run as containers of one Umbrel app (w1kyu-easyarr). Their web UIs open from the
  EasyArr dashboard (http://umbrel.local:39000, apps under /apps/<name>/); Jellyfin is on port
  39096, Jellyseerr on 39055.
- Text like [REDACTED:password] in a user's message was hidden on purpose by EasyArr.
- Source code and issues: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr

This file contains every user guide, generated from docs/ by scripts/llms-txt.mjs.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

This guide takes you from "nothing installed" to "watching your first movie". It takes about
20 minutes, plus the time your first download needs.

> **What you'll need**
>
> - An Umbrel. EasyArr is tested on umbrelOS 2.0. 8 GB of memory or more is best, see
>   [System requirements](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/system-requirements.md).
> - Free disk space for your movies and shows. A movie is often 2–10 GB.
> - A **VPN** subscription. EasyArr only downloads through a VPN. The [VPN guide](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md)
>   helps you pick one. You can also skip it and add it later, but nothing downloads until then.
> - For **Usenet** only: an account with a Usenet provider and one with an indexer, see
>   [Usenet explained](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md). For torrents you don't need any other account.

## 1. Add the w1kyu Apps store to your Umbrel

EasyArr isn't in Umbrel's own App Store. It comes from a "community app store" that you add once.

1. Open your Umbrel in the browser, for example `http://umbrel.local`.
2. Open the **App Store**.
3. Click the **⋯** button at the top right.
4. Click **Community App Stores**.
5. Paste this address: `https://github.com/w1kyu/umbrel-app-store`
6. Click **Add**.

The store is now listed as **w1kyu Apps**. Community stores aren't checked by Umbrel. EasyArr is
open source, so anyone can read its code on [GitHub](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr).

## 2. Install EasyArr

1. Open the **w1kyu Apps** store.
2. Click **EasyArr**, then **Install**.
3. Wait until the EasyArr icon appears on your Umbrel's home screen. The first install downloads
   about a dozen apps, so it can take 5–15 minutes.
4. Click the **EasyArr** icon. The setup starts.

## 3. Go through the setup

The setup asks a few questions, one per page. Every page has a **What's this?** link if you want to
know more. You can go back at any time, and you can change every answer later in **Settings**.

![The first page of the EasyArr setup](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/setup-welcome.jpg)

1. **Welcome.** Press **Start setup**. Already used EasyArr before? Press **Restore from backup**
   instead, see [Backups](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/backup-restore.md).
2. **Checking your Umbrel.** EasyArr looks at your processor, memory, disk and graphics chip. A
   yellow or red result is explained on the page. See [System requirements](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/system-requirements.md).
3. **Create your account.** Choose a username and password. You use them to watch in Jellyfin and
   to request things. Family members get their own accounts later, see
   [Family accounts](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/family-accounts.md).
4. **How do you want to download?** Pick **Torrents**, **Usenet** or **Both**. Not sure? Start with
   torrents. [Torrents 101](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/torrents-101.md) and [Usenet 101](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md) explain the difference.
5. **Protect your downloads with a VPN.** Pick your VPN provider. A short guide for that provider
   opens next to the form: follow it, fill in the fields, then press **Connect**. EasyArr tests the
   connection and checks that your home address is hidden.

   ![The VPN step with the guide on the left and the form on the right](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/setup-vpn.jpg)

6. **Your Usenet accounts** (only for Usenet). Enter your provider and your indexer. EasyArr tests
   both for you.
7. **Add search sites for torrents** (only for torrents). Open Prowlarr from this page and add one
   or more search sites, following [Search sites](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/indexers.md). EasyArr notices them by itself.
8. **What do you want?** Choose movies, shows and/or music, your languages and a quality. The
   default (**Balanced**) suits most people, see [Quality presets](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/quality-presets.md).
9. **Connect everything.** Press **Connect everything**. EasyArr now sets up every app with your
   answers and shows each step as it goes. This takes a minute or two.

When it's done, you see a short "what now" tour. Press **Go to my dashboard**.

![The last setup step when everything is connected, with the three-step tour](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/setup-finish.jpg)

## 4. Ask for your first movie

1. On the EasyArr home screen, press **Request**. The request page (Jellyseerr) opens in a new tab.
2. Sign in with the username and password from step 3 of the setup.
3. Search for a movie and press **Request**.

That's all. EasyArr searches your sites, downloads through the VPN, renames the file and puts it in
your library. You can follow the download on the EasyArr home screen, under **Downloads**.

![The EasyArr home screen with a download in progress](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/home.jpg)

How long it takes depends on the file size, your internet speed and, for torrents, how many people
share the file. Something seems stuck? The home screen tells you why under **Needs your attention**.

## 5. Watch it

1. On the EasyArr home screen, press **Watch**. Jellyfin opens.
2. Sign in with the same username and password.
3. Your movie is under **Movies** once it's downloaded.

On a TV, phone or tablet, install the free **Jellyfin** app from your device's app store. When it
asks for a server, enter `http://umbrel.local:39096`. If that doesn't work, use your Umbrel's IP
address instead, for example `http://192.168.1.20:39096`. Your router's list of connected devices
shows the Umbrel's IP address.

## What next?

- Give your family their own accounts: [Family accounts](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/family-accounts.md).
- Watch when you're away from home: [Remote access with Tailscale](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/remote-access-tailscale.md).
- Turn on automatic backups: [Backups](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/backup-restore.md).
- Something doesn't work? [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md) and [Getting help](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/getting-help.md).

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md -->

# How EasyArr works

EasyArr puts a complete home media setup on your Umbrel and connects all the parts for you. You
don't have to learn any of the apps inside. This page explains what each one does, in case you're
curious.

## The idea in one picture

![How a request travels through EasyArr: request, search, download through the VPN, sort, watch](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/how-it-works.svg)

1. **You ask for something** (a movie, a show or an album) on the request page.
2. **EasyArr's helpers look for it.** Sonarr (shows), Radarr (movies) and Lidarr (music) ask your
   search sites where to get it. Prowlarr manages those sites.
3. **It gets downloaded** with qBittorrent ([torrents](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/torrents-101.md)) or SABnzbd
   ([Usenet](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md)), always through the **VPN**.
4. **It gets sorted** into your library, with clear names, posters and subtitles.
5. **You watch it** in Jellyfin, on your TV, phone or browser.

## The apps inside

**Jellyfin** is your own streaming service. It shows your movies, shows and music with posters and
descriptions, remembers where you stopped, and plays on TVs, phones, tablets and in the browser.
Everyone in your home can have their own account.

**Jellyseerr** is the request page. You search for a movie or show, press **Request**, and it tells
Sonarr or Radarr to get it. It signs you in with your Jellyfin account. It also shows what's
popular and what's coming soon.

**Sonarr** looks after TV shows. It knows every episode of a show, searches for new ones when they
air, and picks the best version that matches your language and quality choices.

**Radarr** does the same for movies.

**Lidarr** does the same for music, by artist and album. Music is requested in Lidarr itself; the
request page only knows movies and shows.

**Prowlarr** keeps the list of your search sites (also called **indexers**). Sonarr, Radarr and
Lidarr ask Prowlarr, and Prowlarr asks all your sites at once. You add the sites once, see
[Search sites](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/indexers.md).

**FlareSolverr** helps Prowlarr with search sites that try to block automated visitors.

**qBittorrent** downloads torrents: files that many people share with each other. See
[Torrents 101](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/torrents-101.md).

**SABnzbd** downloads from Usenet: paid servers that store files. See [Usenet 101](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md).

**Bazarr** finds subtitles in your languages for your movies and shows.

**Recyclarr** keeps the quality settings of Sonarr and Radarr up to date with tried and tested
recommendations from the community ([TRaSH Guides](https://trash-guides.info)).

**Unpackerr** unpacks downloads that arrive as archives (`.rar` files), so they can be added to
your library.

**Cleanuparr** removes downloads that are stuck or broken, so Sonarr and Radarr can try another
version.

**The VPN** (Gluetun) is a secure tunnel to your VPN provider. Every app that goes on the internet to
search or download sends its traffic through it. See [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md).

**The EasyArr dashboard** is the part you see first: the setup, the home screen with your downloads
and warnings, Settings, backups and help. It also connects all the apps to each other with your
answers, and repairs those connections when you ask it to.

## Safety

- **VPN with a kill switch.** All searching and downloading goes through a VPN. If the VPN drops,
  downloads stop instead of using your normal connection. Your home address is never used for
  downloads.
- **Your Umbrel login protects EasyArr.** The dashboard and the apps you open from it (Sonarr,
  Radarr, Prowlarr and the others) can only be reached after you sign in to your Umbrel.
- **Jellyfin and Jellyseerr have their own login**, so family members can use them without your
  Umbrel password. They use the account you created in the setup.
- **Your passwords and keys stay on your Umbrel.** When you ask for help, EasyArr hides them first,
  see [Getting help](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/getting-help.md).

## Where your files are

Everything EasyArr downloads is in **Files → Home → EasyArr** on your Umbrel:

| Folder | What's inside |
| ------ | ------------- |
| `media/movies`, `media/tv`, `media/music` | Your library. Jellyfin shows what's in here. |
| `downloads` | Downloads that aren't finished or sorted yet. |
| `backups` | EasyArr's automatic backups. |

Finished downloads are moved into `media` without using extra disk space. For torrents, the file
stays shared from the same place on the disk (a "hardlink"), so it isn't stored twice.

## Be responsible

Only download content you have the right to download and share. Laws differ between countries.
You are responsible for following the laws where you live.

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/system-requirements.md -->

# System requirements

EasyArr checks your Umbrel during setup. Here's what the results mean.

![The system check in the setup, with a result for each part](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/setup-system.jpg)

## Processor (architecture)

EasyArr runs on the two kinds of processors Umbrel supports:

- **amd64** — Intel and AMD computers (Umbrel Home, most mini PCs and old laptops).
- **arm64** — for example a Raspberry Pi 5.

## Memory (RAM)

EasyArr runs about a dozen apps at the same time.

| RAM          | Result                                                            |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 8 GB or more | ✅ Good                                                           |
| 4–8 GB       | ⚠️ Works, but other Umbrel apps may get slower                    |
| Below 4 GB   | ❌ Not enough. You can continue, but expect apps to crash or stall |

## Free disk space

Movies and shows are big. A movie is often 2–10 GB, a TV season 5–30 GB.
With less than **50 GB** free, EasyArr warns you. Downloads stop when the disk is full.

All your media is stored in **Files → Home → EasyArr** on your Umbrel.

## Graphics (GPU)

Jellyfin sometimes has to convert a video so it plays on a phone or TV (**transcoding**).
A graphics chip (for example Intel Quick Sync) does that quickly.

- **Found** ✅ — Jellyfin can use it for fast transcoding.
- **Not found** ⚠️ — Jellyfin still works. Converting high-quality video will be slow, so pick
  devices that can play your files directly when you can.

Umbrel gives EasyArr access to the graphics chip automatically when your computer has one.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/torrents-101.md -->

# Torrents 101

Torrents are one of two ways EasyArr can download things. The other one is
[Usenet](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md). You can use both.

## How torrents work

1. A file is split into many small pieces.
2. People who have the file share those pieces with each other.
3. Your download client (qBittorrent) collects the pieces from many people at once.
4. While you download, you also share pieces with others. That's called **seeding**.

Nobody runs a central server. That's why torrents cost nothing.

## Where torrents come from

Websites that list torrents are called **indexers** or **trackers**. EasyArr asks them for you
through Prowlarr. You add the indexers yourself later in the setup. EasyArr doesn't recommend
any specific site.

- **Public trackers** are open to everyone. They are easy to start with, but files are
  sometimes fake or slow.
- **Private trackers** need an invite. They are usually faster and cleaner, but have rules
  (for example: share back as much as you download).

## Pros and cons

| 👍 Good                              | 👎 Not so good                                       |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Free                                 | Speed depends on how many people share a file        |
| Huge choice, also old or rare things | Old or rare things can take a long time              |
| No account needed to start           | Everyone sharing a file can see your IP address      |
|                                      | Needs a VPN (EasyArr makes that the default, see below) |

## Why EasyArr needs a VPN for torrents

When you share a file, everyone else sharing it can see your internet address (IP).
A **VPN** hides it. EasyArr sends all download traffic through a VPN and blocks it completely
when the VPN is down (a **kill switch**). You set the VPN up in the next part of the setup.

A VPN with **port forwarding** makes torrents faster, because other people can connect to you
directly.

## Be responsible

Only download content you have the right to download and share. Laws differ between countries
— you are responsible for following yours.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md -->

# Usenet 101

Usenet is one of two ways EasyArr can download things. The other one is
[torrents](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/torrents-101.md). You can use both.

## How Usenet works

Usenet is a very old network of servers (from 1980) that store posted files. You don't share
anything with other people — you simply download from a server, like from a normal website.

To use it you need two things:

1. **A Usenet provider** (paid). That's the server you download from. You get a username,
   a password and a server address. Prices are usually a few euros/dollars per month.
2. **An indexer** (often free or a small yearly fee). That's a search engine that tells EasyArr
   *what* to download from the provider. You get a website address and an **API key**.

SABnzbd is the app in EasyArr that does the actual downloading. You enter both in the setup
(step 6), and EasyArr connects everything for you.

## Setting it up in EasyArr

### Your provider

1. Pick your provider from the list. EasyArr fills in the **server address**, the **port** and
   the number of **connections** for you. (The list just saves typing — it isn't a
   recommendation.) Not in the list? Choose *Other provider* and copy the server address from
   your provider's website (look for "setup", "server settings" or "newsreader").
2. Enter the **username** and **password** of your provider account. Some providers use your
   e-mail address as the username, others give you a separate one — the provider's welcome
   e-mail says which.
3. Keep **SSL** on. It encrypts the connection, so your internet provider can't see what you
   download. The SSL port is almost always **563**.
4. **Connections** is how many parts SABnzbd downloads at the same time. Use what your plan
   allows (the preset does). Too many and the provider refuses you; fewer is just slower.
5. Press **Test this provider**. "It works" means SABnzbd could sign in.

Got a second provider as a backup (a "block account")? Press **Add another provider**.
SABnzbd uses it when the first one is missing something.

### Your indexer

1. Pick your indexer from the list (it comes from Prowlarr) or choose *Other indexer* and enter
   its address, for example `https://indexer.example`.
2. Copy your **API key** from the indexer's website. It's usually on your profile page or a page
   called "API" or "RSS". It's a long code that lets EasyArr search on your behalf.
3. Press **Test this indexer**.

You can add several indexers — more indexers find more.

### Tests fail?

| What EasyArr says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The username, password or API key was refused | Copy it again from your account. Watch out for spaces at the start or end. |
| Couldn't reach this address | Check the server address for typos. Only the name, like `news.example.com` — no `https://`. |
| No answer in time | Check the port (563 with SSL). Some providers also offer 443. |
| Your VPN isn't connected | Tests and downloads go through the VPN. Set it up in step 5 first. |

Passwords and API keys are stored only on your Umbrel. EasyArr never shows them again — leave
the field empty to keep the saved one.

## Pros and cons

| 👍 Good                                             | 👎 Not so good                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Very fast — often as fast as your internet line     | Costs money (provider)                         |
| You don't share anything with others                | You need two accounts (provider + indexer)     |
| Your IP address isn't visible to other people       | Very old or rare things may be missing          |
| Reliable: no waiting for other people to come online | A little more to set up at the start          |

## Torrents or Usenet?

- **Just trying things out?** Start with **torrents**. They cost nothing.
- **Want fast and reliable downloads, and don't mind paying a little?** Choose **Usenet**.
- **Want the best of both?** Choose **both**. EasyArr then searches both and takes whichever
  has what you asked for.

You can change your choice later in Settings.

## Be responsible

Only download content you have the right to download. Laws differ between countries — you are
responsible for following yours.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/indexers.md -->

# Adding search sites (indexers) in Prowlarr

EasyArr finds torrents through **Prowlarr**. Prowlarr asks the search sites you choose, and shares
them with Sonarr (shows), Radarr (movies) and Lidarr (music) by itself — you add each site only
once, in Prowlarr.

EasyArr doesn't choose, rank or recommend sites. Which sites you use — and what you download —
is up to you. Only download content you have the right to download and share.

**Needs the VPN:** Prowlarr checks every site when you add it, through the VPN. If you skipped the
VPN, set it up first (setup step 5) or add your sites later.

## Step by step

![The search-sites step in the setup: the steps on the left, Open Prowlarr and Check again](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/setup-indexers.jpg)

1. In the setup, press **Open Prowlarr**. Prowlarr opens in a new tab — you're already signed in.
2. On the **Indexers** page, press **Add Indexer** (or **Add New Indexer** when the list is still
   empty).
3. A long list of sites appears. Type the name of a site you use into the search box, or narrow
   the list with the filters:
   - **Protocol**: `torrent` for torrent sites.
   - **Privacy**: **Public** sites are open to everyone; **Private** and **Semi-Private** sites
     need an account (often by invite).
   - **Language**: sites in your language.
4. Click the site. A form opens.
   - **Public site**: usually nothing to fill in.
   - **Private site**: enter what the form asks for — usually your **Username** and **Password**,
     an **API Key**, or a **Cookie** from that site. The site's own help pages say where to find it.
5. Press **Test**. A green check means Prowlarr can reach the site.
6. Press **Save**.
7. Want more? Add another one the same way. Two or three sites are a good start.
8. Come back to EasyArr. It notices the new sites by itself (or press **Check again**).

That's it: Prowlarr hands the sites to Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr within a minute.

## "Blocked by CloudFlare Protection"

Some sites sit behind Cloudflare's bot check. Prowlarr then says
*"Unable to access …, blocked by CloudFlare Protection."* EasyArr includes **FlareSolverr**,
which solves that check for Prowlarr:

1. In the site's form, find **Tags**.
2. Type `flaresolverr` and pick it from the list.
3. Press **Test** again, then **Save**.

Only sites with that tag go through FlareSolverr (it's slower, so not all of them do).

## Something doesn't work?

| Prowlarr says                              | What to do                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Unable to connect" or a time-out          | Check that the VPN is connected (EasyArr home screen). Try again later — sites go down sometimes. |
| "blocked by CloudFlare Protection"         | Add the `flaresolverr` tag (see above).                                   |
| Login / API key / cookie refused            | Copy it again from the site. Cookies expire — get a fresh one.            |
| The site isn't in the list                  | Prowlarr only lists sites it supports. Pick another one.                  |

## Usenet indexers

Using Usenet? You enter your Usenet indexers in EasyArr's setup (step 6) instead, and EasyArr adds
them to Prowlarr for you. See [Usenet 101](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/quality-presets.md -->

# Quality presets

In the setup's "What do you want?" step you pick one of three presets. It decides which versions
EasyArr looks for and how much disk space your library takes. You can switch later; files you
already have stay as they are.

| Preset | Movies and shows | Music | Roughly per movie | per hour of TV | per album |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Best quality** | 4K (2160p) from streaming services when it exists, otherwise 1080p | Lossless (FLAC) | 15–30 GB | 4–12 GB | 300–600 MB |
| **Balanced** (default) | 1080p from Blu-ray or streaming services | High-quality MP3/AAC, upgraded to lossless when available | 6–15 GB | 1.5–4 GB | 100–600 MB |
| **Save space** | 1080p, preferring smaller files | High-quality MP3/AAC | 3–8 GB | 1–2 GB | 80–150 MB |

Sizes are rough averages — a three-hour film is bigger than a short one, and animation is
usually smaller.

## Which one should I pick?

![The "What do you want?" step: libraries, languages and the three quality presets](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/setup-library.jpg)

- **Balanced** suits most people: sharp on a big TV, and a 4 TB disk holds a few hundred movies.
- **Best quality** if you have a 4K TV and plenty of storage. Not every movie or show exists
  in 4K — then EasyArr takes 1080p, so nothing stays missing.
- **Save space** for phones, tablets, laptops or a small disk.

Your Umbrel's home screen and Settings show how much space is free.

## What EasyArr sets up

- **Shows and movies:** EasyArr uses [Recyclarr](https://recyclarr.dev) to create a quality
  profile in Sonarr and Radarr from the [TRaSH guides](https://trash-guides.info) — a community
  guide to good releases. The profile is called **"EasyArr (Best quality)"**, **"EasyArr
  (Balanced)"** or **"EasyArr (Save space)"**.
  - Best quality: TRaSH profiles *WEB-2160p* (shows) and *WEBDL 2160p* (movies), both with a
    1080p fallback.
  - Balanced: *WEB-1080p* (shows) and *HD Bluray + WEB* (movies).
  - Save space: *WEB-1080p* (shows) and *WEB 1080p* (movies), with sizes leaning to the small end.
- **Two changes to the TRaSH profiles:**
  - Releases from groups the guide calls low quality (for example YTS) aren't blocked. They're a
    last resort: EasyArr takes one only when nothing better exists at the same resolution, and
    replaces it automatically when a better version shows up. On public torrent sites they're often
    the only releases there are, and without them your request would just stay "Missing".
  - Balanced movies: 1080p from Blu-ray and from streaming services count as the same quality, so
    the release's score decides. Otherwise a low-quality "Blu-ray" would beat a good streaming
    release.
- **Music:** EasyArr creates its own Lidarr profile with the same name.

## Languages

In the setup you pick two lists, each best first:

- **Audio** (what you hear), for example 1. German, 2. Original language, 3. English. "Original
  language" means the language the film or show was made in.
- **Subtitles** (what you read), for example 1. German, 2. English. The list may be empty.

Any language can be marked **Must have**:

- **Audio must-haves:** a file needs at least one of them. If none of them is available, EasyArr
  doesn't download anything else without asking you. Without must-haves any language is fine and
  the order only says what you prefer.
- **Subtitle must-haves:** downloads don't wait for subtitles. Bazarr keeps looking, and the home
  screen shows which movies and episodes are still missing them.

What each app does with this:

- **Sonarr and Radarr:** EasyArr adds its own "EasyArr – Language: …" rules. A release in your first
  audio language scores highest, the next one a bit less, and so on. Quality still comes first: a
  1080p release in your second language beats a 720p one in your first. When a better-ranked language
  shows up at the same quality, it replaces the file automatically.
- **Bazarr:** looks for subtitles in your subtitle languages, in that order.
- **Jellyfin:** plays your first audio language when a file has several, shows your first subtitle
  language when the audio is in another language, and uses that language for titles and descriptions.
- **Request page (Jellyseerr):** has no language setting of its own. Requests use the EasyArr
  profiles above, so they follow your languages too.

If you installed EasyArr before this, your lists now read: audio "Original language, then (the
language you chose)", subtitles "(the language you chose)", nothing marked as must-have. Change them
in **Settings → Libraries & quality**.

## Whole seasons and trying again

- **Whole seasons:** when you ask for a show or a season that's already finished, Sonarr searches
  season by season, and EasyArr's profile gives a whole-season pack a bonus over single episodes.
  Seasons that are still airing come episode by episode. A season pack alone never makes EasyArr
  download episodes you already have again.
- **Trying again:** if nothing was found when you asked for something, EasyArr asks Sonarr and
  Radarr to search again every 6 hours, a few items at a time so your search sites don't block you.
  Change how often (or switch it off) in **Settings → Advanced**. It pauses while the VPN is down
  or every search site is unreachable.

## When something doesn't arrive

If a movie or episode you asked for still hasn't started downloading after about 12 hours, EasyArr
asks Sonarr or Radarr why and shows it under **Needs your OK** on the home screen, in plain words,
with a button where there's a way out:

- Only available in a language you didn't mark as a must-have → **Download in English** (or
  whichever language exists).
- Only a lower quality exists → **Accept 720p** (cinema recordings are never offered).
- Every version failed before → **Try the best one again**.
- Nothing found, or nobody is sharing it → **Search now** (EasyArr also keeps looking by itself).
- A download got stuck or couldn't be added to your library → **Try another version**.
- Your request didn't reach Sonarr or Radarr → **Send it again**.

Nothing switches to another language or quality unless you click. If you'd rather not be asked,
turn on **Settings → Advanced → Accept alternatives automatically**: EasyArr then takes the best
other version itself and tells you on the home screen. Problems with the whole setup (VPN down,
search sites unreachable, disk full, an app not answering) show in the warnings at the top instead.

## Want to fine-tune?

EasyArr owns the "EasyArr (…)" profiles and resets them when it updates them. To customise, open
Sonarr or Radarr → **Settings → Profiles**, clone the EasyArr profile, edit the copy and use that
one instead.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md -->

# VPN basics

_Last checked: 31 October 2026_

EasyArr only downloads through a **VPN**. This page explains what that means, why it matters, and
how to choose a provider. Each provider has its own step-by-step guide (links below).

## What is a VPN?

Normally, every website and every person you exchange data with sees your **IP address**. That's
the internet address of your home. Your internet provider can see what you connect to.

A **VPN** (virtual private network) is a service you pay for (a few euros/dollars per month).
It creates a locked tunnel from your Umbrel to one of the VPN's servers. Your traffic leaves the
internet from **there**, not from your home. So:

- other people see the **VPN server's address**, not yours,
- your internet provider only sees that you talk to a VPN — not what you download.

## Why EasyArr needs one

With [torrents](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/torrents-101.md), everyone who shares the same file can see the address of
everyone else. Copyright companies watch torrents and collect these addresses. Without a VPN,
that would be your home address — and your internet provider could send you a letter or a fine.

With [Usenet](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md), nobody else sees you, but your internet provider still sees what
you download. A VPN hides that too.

That's why EasyArr sends **all** download traffic through the VPN: Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr,
Prowlarr, qBittorrent and SABnzbd. Jellyfin and Jellyseerr (watching and requesting) don't use the
VPN, so streaming at home stays fast.

## The kill switch

A VPN connection can drop — for example when the VPN server restarts. Many apps then quietly carry
on over your normal connection. EasyArr doesn't.

The **kill switch** blocks **all** internet traffic of the download apps whenever the VPN isn't
connected. Downloads simply pause, and they continue by themselves once the VPN is back. Your home
address is never used for downloading, not even for a second.

## "Your home IP is hidden"

After you connect, EasyArr runs a **connection test** and shows:

![A passed connection test: the VPN's address and country, home IP hidden, port forwarding on](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/setup-vpn-connected.jpg)

- **The VPN's address and country** — that's where your downloads appear to come from.
- **"Your home IP is hidden"** — EasyArr also looks up your real home address (outside the VPN)
  and compares the two. If they're different, the VPN is protecting you. If they're the same,
  EasyArr warns you and keeps downloads blocked.
- **Port forwarding** — on or off, and which port (see below).

Sometimes EasyArr can't look up your home address (that check needs the internet outside the VPN).
It then says so. The VPN itself is still connected and the kill switch still works.

## Port forwarding in plain words

With a VPN, other people can't start a connection **to** you — only you can connect to them.
For torrents, that means you can only exchange data with people who accept incoming connections.
You find fewer people to share with, and downloads are slower. Rare files may not finish at all.

**Port forwarding** opens one "door" (a **port**) on the VPN server that leads to you. Now other
people can connect to you too: more people to share with, faster torrents, better ratios on
private trackers.

- **Automatic:** some providers hand out a port when you connect. EasyArr picks it up and sets it
  in qBittorrent for you.
- **Reserved:** with AirVPN you reserve a port in your account once and enter it in EasyArr.
  EasyArr sets it in qBittorrent.
- **Usenet doesn't need port forwarding at all.** If you only use Usenet, any provider is fine.

Without port forwarding, torrents still work — just slower.

## Which provider?

This isn't a ranking. Every provider below works with EasyArr. If you use torrents, port
forwarding is the one feature that really makes a difference.

| Provider                      | Port forwarding                          | Guide                           |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Proton VPN                    | Yes, automatic (paid plans only)         | [Proton VPN](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/protonvpn.md)      |
| Private Internet Access (PIA) | Yes, automatic                           | [PIA](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/pia.md)                   |
| AirVPN                        | Yes, a port you reserve yourself         | [AirVPN](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/airvpn.md)             |
| PrivateVPN                    | Yes, automatic                           | [Other providers](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/generic.md)   |
| Perfect Privacy               | Yes, automatic                           | [Other providers](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/generic.md)   |
| Mullvad                       | No                                       | [Mullvad](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/mullvad.md)           |
| NordVPN                       | No                                       | [NordVPN](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/nordvpn.md)           |
| Surfshark                     | No                                       | [Surfshark](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/surfshark.md)       |
| Other providers in the list   | No                                       | [Other providers](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/generic.md)   |
| Not in the list               | Only a fixed port your provider gave you | [Custom config file](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/custom.md) |

Already have a VPN? Use the one you have. Prices, server locations and features change often —
check the provider's website before you buy.

## WireGuard or OpenVPN?

These are two ways to build the VPN tunnel. Some providers offer both, some only one. If you can
choose, pick **WireGuard**: it's faster, connects in seconds, and usually needs just one key
instead of a username and password. **OpenVPN** is older and works everywhere; it's the fallback
when your provider has no WireGuard option. Both are equally safe with EasyArr's kill switch.

## Free plans

**Proton VPN** has a free plan, and EasyArr supports it ("I use the free plan"). It works, with
limits:

- no port forwarding,
- only a few server countries, and they're often busy,
- Proton doesn't allow torrent (P2P) traffic on free servers.

So the free plan is good for **Usenet** or for trying EasyArr out. For torrents you need a paid
plan. EasyArr's free-plan option is only for Proton VPN; free tiers of other providers usually have
data limits that make downloading impractical.

## "Skip for now"

You can skip the VPN step in the setup. Nothing leaks: the kill switch is already on. But until you
connect a VPN, the download apps can't reach the internet at all, so **nothing downloads**.
Jellyfin, Jellyseerr and everything already in your library keep working.

Add the VPN later in **Settings → VPN**.

## Changing provider later

Open **Settings → VPN**, pick the new provider, fill in the fields and press **Connect**. EasyArr
runs the connection test again. No reinstall, and your library and settings stay as they are.
Keys and passwords are stored only on your Umbrel and are never shown again. If you keep the same
provider and only change, say, the server location, you can leave the saved fields empty.

## Be responsible

A VPN protects your privacy. It doesn't make downloading things you have no right to legal. Only
download content you have the right to download and share. Laws differ between countries — you are
responsible for following yours.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/protonvpn.md -->

# Proton VPN — set up in EasyArr

_Last checked: 31 October 2026_

Proton VPN is in the **Best for torrents** group: with a paid plan, EasyArr gets a forwarded port
from Proton automatically and puts it into qBittorrent for you.

## What you need

- A Proton VPN account. The **free plan connects**, but it only uses Proton's free servers, has
  **no port forwarding**, and Proton **doesn't allow torrents (P2P) on free servers**. It's fine
  for Usenet. The free plan also covers only one device at a time.
- For **port forwarding** (faster, more reliable torrents): **any paid Proton VPN plan**, for
  example VPN Plus. EasyArr then only uses Proton's **P2P servers** (servers that allow file
  sharing) — it picks them for you.
- A web browser to sign in at [account.protonvpn.com](https://account.protonvpn.com/login).

**Port forwarding** means other people sharing a file can connect to you directly, not only you
to them. **WireGuard** and **OpenVPN** are two ways of connecting to a VPN. WireGuard is newer
and faster, so EasyArr recommends it.

## Option A: WireGuard (recommended)

You need one value: a **private key**. It is a secret code of 44 characters that ends with `=`.

1. Sign in at [account.protonvpn.com](https://account.protonvpn.com/login) with your normal
   Proton login.
2. In the menu, open **Downloads**, then the **WireGuard configuration** section.
3. Type any name for the configuration, for example `EasyArr`.
4. Under **Platform**, pick any option (for example **Router** or **GNU/Linux**). It doesn't
   matter for EasyArr.
5. Under the **VPN options**:
   - **Paid plan:** switch **NAT-PMP (Port Forwarding)** **on**. Without it, port forwarding
     can't work later.
   - Leave **Moderate NAT** **off** — Proton says it can't be used together with port forwarding.
   - **Free plan:** you only see **VPN Accelerator**. That's fine, leave it as it is.
6. Pick any server. EasyArr chooses its own server later — the key works for all of them. (Proton
   suggests a P2P server, shown with a double-arrow icon ⇄, if you want to follow its guide
   exactly.)
7. Click **Create**. Wait a few seconds until the configuration appears.
8. Click **Download** to save the file (it ends in `.conf`). Open it with a text editor
   (Notepad, TextEdit…).
9. Find the line that starts with `PrivateKey =`. Copy everything **after** `PrivateKey =`. That
   is your WireGuard private key.

Keep this file private: anyone who has the key can use your VPN. If you lose it, simply create a
new configuration.

## Option B: OpenVPN

You need a **VPN username** and **VPN password**. These are special OpenVPN credentials that
Proton creates for you. They are **not** your normal Proton login (email + password).

1. Sign in at [account.protonvpn.com](https://account.protonvpn.com/login) with your normal
   Proton login.
2. In the menu on the left, open **Account**.
3. Find the section **OpenVPN / IKEv2 username** (Proton sometimes just calls it "OpenVPN
   username").
4. Copy the **username** and the **password** shown there.

You do **not** need to download any OpenVPN files — EasyArr already knows Proton's servers.

## Fill in EasyArr

1. In the VPN step, pick **Proton VPN** (group **Best for torrents**).
2. **Connection type:** choose **WireGuard** (if you did Option A) or **OpenVPN** (Option B).
3. Fill in the fields:

| EasyArr field         | What to paste                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| WireGuard private key | WireGuard only: the text after `PrivateKey =` from your `.conf` file |
| VPN username          | OpenVPN only: your OpenVPN / IKEv2 username from the Account page   |
| VPN password          | OpenVPN only: your OpenVPN / IKEv2 password from the Account page   |

4. **I use the free plan:** tick it **only** if you have the free plan. EasyArr then uses only
   free servers and turns port forwarding off.
5. **Server country** (optional): leave **Fastest / any** unless you want a specific country.
6. **Port forwarding:** leave it **on** (the default) if you have a paid plan.
7. Press **Connect** and wait for the test.

Good to know:

- With WireGuard you don't need an address — EasyArr uses Proton's standard one (`10.2.0.2/32`).
- With OpenVPN and port forwarding on, Proton wants `+pmp` added to the end of the username.
  **EasyArr adds it for you.** Paste the username exactly as Proton shows it.

## If the test fails

- **"The key isn't right" or "Couldn't reach the VPN server" (WireGuard):** copy the key again —
  all 44 characters, with the `=` at the end and no spaces. Still failing? Create a new
  configuration in your Proton account and use its key.
- **"Username or password was refused" (OpenVPN):** you probably used your normal Proton login.
  Use the OpenVPN / IKEv2 username and password from the **Account** page instead. Also check
  your plan is still active.
- **Connected, but no forwarded port appears:** your WireGuard key was made without **NAT-PMP
  (Port Forwarding)**, or you're on the free plan. Create a new configuration with NAT-PMP
  switched on (paid plan only) and paste the new key.
- **"No server matches your choice":** choose **Fastest / any** as server country. Free plans
  only have servers in a few countries.

Back to [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/pia.md -->

# Private Internet Access (PIA) — set up in EasyArr

_Last checked: 31 October 2026_

PIA is in EasyArr's **Best for torrents** group: it has **automatic port forwarding**, which
makes torrents faster. EasyArr connects to PIA with **OpenVPN**. (PIA's WireGuard needs an extra
login step that EasyArr's VPN part doesn't support yet. OpenVPN is just as safe.)

PIA is one of the easiest providers to set up: you only need your normal PIA login. No keys, no
files.

## What you need

- An active, paid PIA subscription.
- Your **PIA username**. It's the letter `p` followed by 7 digits, like `p1234567`. It is **not**
  your email address.
- Your **PIA password** (the one you also use in the PIA app).

## Find your username and password

1. Search your email inbox for the message PIA sent when you bought your subscription. It
   contains your username and password.
2. Can't find it? Your username is also shown in the PIA app under **Settings → Account**.
3. Forgot your password? Reset it on PIA's website at
   `privateinternetaccess.com/account/reset-password`.
4. To double-check both, log in to your account on **privateinternetaccess.com** with them. If
   that works, EasyArr will accept them too.

PIA's help pages sometimes call these your "VPN service credentials". For OpenVPN that's the same
`p1234567` username and your account password. (A username starting with `x` is PIA's separate
proxy login — don't use it here.)

## Port forwarding — what to know

- In EasyArr, **Port forwarding** is **on** by default for PIA. You don't need to change anything
  in your PIA account.
- Each time EasyArr connects, it asks PIA for a port and puts it into qBittorrent for you. If PIA
  hands out a new port later, EasyArr updates qBittorrent automatically.
- **PIA doesn't offer port forwarding on its US server locations** (PIA's help pages, checked
  31 October 2026). While the switch is on, EasyArr only lists regions that support port
  forwarding, and **Fastest / any** only uses those. Right now that's every region outside the US.
- Need a US server? Turn **Port forwarding** off. Torrents still work, just slower.
- Only use Usenet? Port forwarding doesn't matter for you. You can leave it on or off.

## Fill in EasyArr

1. In the VPN step of the setup (or later in **Settings → VPN**), choose **Private Internet
   Access (PIA)** in the **Best for torrents** group. The connection type is **OpenVPN**.
2. Fill in the fields:

| EasyArr field       | What to enter                                             |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| **VPN username**    | Your PIA username, like `p1234567`                        |
| **VPN password**    | Your PIA password                                         |
| **Port forwarding** | Leave it **on** (recommended for torrents)                |
| **Server region**   | Optional: a region close to you, or **Fastest / any**     |

3. Press **Connect**. EasyArr tests the connection. You should see **Connected to Private Internet
   Access (PIA)**, **Your home IP is hidden** and **Port forwarding is on (port …)**.
4. If it says **Waiting for your VPN to hand out a port…**, give it a minute. PIA usually sends
   the port within a few seconds of connecting.

## If the test fails

- **"Username or password was refused":** you entered your email address instead of the
  `p1234567` username, or there's a typo in the password. Check both by logging in on
  privateinternetaccess.com, and make sure your subscription is active.
- **"No server matches your choice" or "Pick a location from the list":** the region you picked
  has no port forwarding (all US regions, for example). Choose **Fastest / any** or another
  region, or turn port forwarding off.
- **Port forwarding keeps waiting:** pick another region and press **Connect** again. Some
  regions are busy now and then.
- **"Couldn't reach the VPN server":** that PIA region may be down for a moment. Try another
  region or **Fastest / any**.

Back to [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/airvpn.md -->

# AirVPN — set up in EasyArr

_Last checked: 31 October 2026_

AirVPN is in EasyArr's **Best for torrents** group. Its port forwarding works a little
differently: you **reserve a port once** in your AirVPN account and type it into EasyArr. EasyArr
then sets it in qBittorrent for you. You can connect with **WireGuard** (recommended — faster and
simpler) or **OpenVPN**. You only need one of them.

## What you need

- An active, paid AirVPN subscription.
- A computer with a web browser and a simple text editor (Notepad on Windows, TextEdit on Mac).
- About 10 minutes.

All steps below happen on **airvpn.org** after you **Sign In**, in the **Client Area** (top menu).

## Step 1: Create a "device" for EasyArr (recommended)

AirVPN calls each set of keys a **device**. Giving EasyArr its own device avoids clashes with your
computer or phone: two connections with the same key can't use the same AirVPN server at once.

1. Open **Client Area → Devices**.
2. Click **Add a new device**. Give it a name you'll recognise, like `EasyArr` (click the pencil
   icon to edit the name).

## Step 2a: WireGuard values (recommended)

1. Open **Client Area → Config Generator**.
2. As the operating system, choose **Linux** (that's what EasyArr runs on).
3. Under the protocols, tick a **WireGuard** entry.
4. Choose your **EasyArr** device.
5. Pick any one server or country. It doesn't matter — you choose the server country in EasyArr.
6. Accept the Terms of Service and click **Generate**. Download the `.conf` file.
7. Open the file with your text editor. You need three lines:

| Line in the file                   | What it is                                 |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `PrivateKey = …` (near the top)    | Your private key (44 characters, ends in `=`) |
| `PresharedKey = …` (further down)  | An extra shared secret (also ends in `=`)  |
| `Address = 10.x.x.x/32, …`         | Your VPN-internal address                  |

Don't use the `PublicKey` line — that belongs to the AirVPN server. On the `Address` line, you
only need the first part, like `10.128.45.67/32`. The longer part after the comma is IPv6 (a newer
kind of internet address); EasyArr ignores it.

## Step 2b: OpenVPN values

1. Open **Client Area → Config Generator**.
2. Choose **Linux**, tick an **OpenVPN** entry (UDP is fine), and choose your **EasyArr** device.
3. Pick any one server or country, accept the Terms of Service and click **Generate**. Download
   the `.ovpn` file. Leave the advanced options as they are.
4. Open the file with your text editor. It contains several blocks. Ignore the `<ca>` and
   `<tls-crypt>` blocks. You need two:
   - everything between `<cert>` and `</cert>` — your **client certificate**,
   - everything between `<key>` and `</key>` — your **client key**.

## Step 3: Reserve a port (for torrents)

1. Open **Client Area → Ports** (the page is called **Forwarded ports**).
2. Add a new port. Leave the port number empty to let AirVPN pick a free one, or type one
   (AirVPN uses ports from 2048 upwards).
3. Choose **TCP & UDP**. Leave the **Local** field **empty** — torrent ports must not be mapped
   to a different number.
4. Under **Device**, choose **All Devices** or your **EasyArr** device. If you choose a device,
   it must be the same one you generated the file with, or the port won't reach EasyArr.
5. Save it and write down the port number.

The port stays yours as long as your subscription is active. Don't also open this port on your
home router — AirVPN warns that this can leak traffic outside the VPN. Only use Usenet? You can
skip this step.

## Fill in EasyArr

1. In the VPN step of the setup (or later in **Settings → VPN**), choose **AirVPN** in the **Best
   for torrents** group.
2. Under **Connection type**, choose **WireGuard** or **OpenVPN** — the same one you prepared.
3. Fill in the fields:

| Connection type | EasyArr field               | What to paste                                   |
| --------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| WireGuard       | **WireGuard private key**   | The value after `PrivateKey =`                  |
| WireGuard       | **WireGuard preshared key** | The value after `PresharedKey =`                |
| WireGuard       | **WireGuard address**       | The first part of the `Address` line, e.g. `10.128.45.67/32` |
| OpenVPN         | **Client certificate**      | The text between `<cert>` and `</cert>`         |
| OpenVPN         | **Client key**              | The text between `<key>` and `</key>`           |

4. Turn **Port forwarding** on and type your port into **Your reserved port** (EasyArr accepts
   1024–65535).
5. **Server country** (optional): pick one close to you, or leave **Fastest / any**.
6. Press **Connect**. You should see **Connected to AirVPN**, **Your home IP is hidden** and
   **Port forwarding is on (port …)**.

## If the test fails

- **"The key isn't right" or "Couldn't reach the VPN server" (WireGuard):** a key was pasted into
  the wrong field (private and preshared mixed up, or the server's `PublicKey` used). Also, if you
  renewed or deleted the device under **Devices**, its old keys stop working — generate a new file.
- **"The certificate or key wasn't accepted" (OpenVPN):** you probably copied the `<ca>` or
  `<tls-crypt>` block. Copy the `<cert>` and `<key>` blocks again from a freshly generated file.
- **Connected, but torrents stay slow:** check the port on the **Forwarded ports** page — same
  number as in EasyArr, **Local** empty, and **Device** set to **All Devices** or your EasyArr
  device.
- **Connection drops when your computer uses AirVPN too:** both use the same device. Create a
  separate EasyArr device (Step 1) and generate new values with it.

Back to [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/mullvad.md -->

# Mullvad — set up in EasyArr

_Last checked: 31 October 2026_

Mullvad is in the **Also works** group. It is safe and simple, but it has **no port forwarding**
(Mullvad removed it in 2023). Torrents still work, just slower. For Usenet that makes no
difference.

## What you need

- A Mullvad account with time on it (Mullvad has no free plan). Your login is a 16-digit
  **account number** — there is no email or password.
- A free **device slot**: Mullvad allows **5 devices** per account, and EasyArr counts as one.
  If all 5 are used, remove an old one on the **Devices** page of your Mullvad account first.
- A web browser to sign in at [mullvad.net](https://mullvad.net/en/account/login).

Mullvad only supports **WireGuard** (a modern, fast way to connect to a VPN). It switched off
OpenVPN on 15 January 2026, so EasyArr only offers WireGuard for Mullvad.

## Get your key and address

You need two values from one small file: a **private key** (a secret code of 44 characters ending
with `=`) and an **address** (looks like `10.64.123.45/32`).

1. Open Mullvad's [WireGuard configuration generator](https://mullvad.net/en/account/wireguard-config).
2. Log in by entering your Mullvad **account number**.
3. Under **Platform**, pick any option (for example **Linux** or **Router**). It doesn't matter for
   EasyArr.
4. Click **Generate key**. This creates a new key just for EasyArr and uses one device slot.
5. Pick any country, city or server. EasyArr chooses its own server later — the key works for all
   of them.
6. Leave everything else as it is. Click **Download file** and wait a few seconds.
7. Open the downloaded file with a text editor (Notepad, TextEdit…). If you got a `.zip` file,
   open it first and pick any one file inside.
8. Find these two lines near the top:
   - `PrivateKey = …` — copy everything after `PrivateKey =`.
   - `Address = …` — copy only the **first** part, before the comma. It looks like
     `10.64.123.45/32`.

The `Address` line usually also has a second, longer address with colons (`fc00:…`). That's
IPv6, a newer kind of address. EasyArr doesn't use it, so you can leave it out — or paste the
whole line, EasyArr ignores the IPv6 part.

Keep the file private: anyone who has the key can use your Mullvad account.

**Don't** use the "WireGuard key" shown on Mullvad's **Devices** page. That is the public half of
the key and won't work.

## Fill in EasyArr

1. In the VPN step, pick **Mullvad** (group **Also works**).
2. **Connection type** is WireGuard — there is nothing else to choose.
3. Fill in the fields:

| EasyArr field         | What to paste                                                  |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| WireGuard private key | The text after `PrivateKey =` from your file                  |
| WireGuard address     | The first address from the `Address` line, e.g. `10.64.123.45/32` |

4. **Server country** (optional): leave **Fastest / any** unless you want a specific country.
5. Press **Connect** and wait for the test.

The key and address belong together. If you generate a new key, copy the new address too.

## If the test fails

- **"The key isn't right" or "Couldn't reach the VPN server":** copy the key again — all 44
  characters, with the `=` at the end and no spaces. Make sure key and address come from the
  **same** file.
- **The device was removed:** if you (or Mullvad, when you hit the 5-device limit) removed this
  device on the **Devices** page, its key stops working. Generate a new key and paste both new
  values.
- **No time left on the account:** check your account page. Mullvad stops connecting as soon as
  the paid time runs out.
- **"Enter an IPv4 address like 10.64.222.21/32":** you pasted only the IPv6 part. Use the part
  that starts with `10.`.

Back to [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/nordvpn.md -->

# NordVPN — set up in EasyArr

_Last checked: 31 October 2026_

NordVPN is in the **Also works** group. It is safe and fast, but it has **no port forwarding**.
Torrents still work, just slower. For Usenet that makes no difference.

## What you need

- An active NordVPN subscription (any plan).
- Access to the email address of your Nord Account: Nord sends you a **verification code** before
  it shows the manual setup details.
- A web browser to sign in at [my.nordaccount.com](https://my.nordaccount.com/).

**WireGuard** and **OpenVPN** are two ways of connecting to a VPN. WireGuard is newer and faster,
so EasyArr recommends it. NordVPN calls its WireGuard version **NordLynx**.

## Option A: WireGuard (recommended)

You need one value: a **private key**. It is a secret code of 44 characters that ends with `=`.
NordVPN puts it into a WireGuard file you can download.

1. Sign in at [my.nordaccount.com](https://my.nordaccount.com/) and click **NordVPN**.
2. Scroll down to **Advanced settings** and click **Set up NordVPN manually**.
3. If asked, click **Verify email** and enter the code Nord sends you.
4. Open the **Server recommendation** tab. Take the recommended server or pick any other one —
   EasyArr chooses its own server later. If you can, pick one with a **Verified** badge.
5. Click **Get setup configuration** (on some pages: **WireGuard** under **Available protocols**).
6. Choose **WireGuard** and click **Download config**. You get a file ending in `.conf`.
7. Open the file with a text editor (Notepad, TextEdit…).
8. Find the line that starts with `PrivateKey =`. Copy everything **after** `PrivateKey =`. That
   is your WireGuard private key.

You don't need the other lines. EasyArr already knows NordVPN's servers and its standard address
(`10.5.0.2/32`).

Keep this file private: anyone who has the key can use your NordVPN account.

## Option B: OpenVPN

You need a **VPN username** and **VPN password**. NordVPN calls them **service credentials**.
They are **not** your Nord Account email and password.

1. Sign in at [my.nordaccount.com](https://my.nordaccount.com/) and click **NordVPN**.
2. Scroll down to **Advanced settings** and click **Set up NordVPN manually**.
3. Open the **Service credentials** tab.
4. Click **Verify email** and enter the code Nord sends you.
5. Copy the **Username** and the **Password** with the **Copy** buttons next to them.

You do **not** need to download any OpenVPN files — EasyArr already knows NordVPN's servers.

## Fill in EasyArr

1. In the VPN step, pick **NordVPN** (group **Also works**).
2. **Connection type:** choose **WireGuard** (if you did Option A) or **OpenVPN** (Option B).
3. Fill in the fields:

| EasyArr field         | What to paste                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| WireGuard private key | WireGuard only: the text after `PrivateKey =` from your `.conf` file |
| VPN username          | OpenVPN only: the service credentials **Username**                  |
| VPN password          | OpenVPN only: the service credentials **Password**                  |

4. **Server country** (optional): leave **Fastest / any** unless you want a specific country.
5. Press **Connect** and wait for the test.

## If the test fails

- **"The key isn't right" or "Couldn't reach the VPN server" (WireGuard):** copy the key again —
  all 44 characters, with the `=` at the end and no spaces. Still failing? Download a fresh
  WireGuard file from the **Set up NordVPN manually** page and use its key.
- **"Username or password was refused" (OpenVPN):** you probably used your Nord Account email and
  password. Use the **service credentials** instead. Copy them with the **Copy** buttons so no
  space sneaks in.
- **Subscription ended:** check in your Nord Account that your NordVPN plan is still active.
- **"No server matches your choice":** choose **Fastest / any** as server country, or try another
  country.

Back to [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/surfshark.md -->

# Surfshark — set up in EasyArr

_Last checked: 31 October 2026_

Surfshark works well with EasyArr. It has **no port forwarding**, so torrents work but can be a
bit slower. Usenet isn't affected at all. You can connect in two ways: **WireGuard**
(recommended — faster and simpler) or **OpenVPN**. You only need one of them.

## What you need

- An active, paid Surfshark subscription.
- A computer or phone with a web browser.
- For WireGuard: a simple text editor to open a small file (Notepad on Windows, TextEdit on Mac).
- About 5 minutes.

## WireGuard (recommended): get your key and address

WireGuard needs two values: a **private key** (a secret password-like code, 44 characters ending
in `=`) and an **address** (your VPN-internal address, looks like `10.14.0.2/16`).

1. Go to **surfshark.com** and log in to your account.
2. Open **VPN → Manual setup**. (On some screens it's **Products → VPN → Manual setup**.)
3. Choose **Desktop or mobile**, then **WireGuard**.
4. Choose **I don't have a key pair**. Type a name you'll recognise, like `EasyArr`, and continue.
5. Click **Generate a new key pair**. Surfshark now shows a **Public key** and a **Private key**.
6. Copy the **Private key** and keep it somewhere safe, for example in your password manager.
   Surfshark shows it only this once.
7. Click **Choose a location**, pick any location and press **Download**. You get a small file
   ending in `.conf` (for example `de-fra.conf`).
   - Always create the key pair **before** you download. Otherwise the file is missing your key.
   - The location doesn't matter. You pick the server country in EasyArr later.
8. Open the `.conf` file with your text editor. Find the line that starts with `Address`, for
   example `Address = 10.14.0.2/16`. Copy the part that looks like `10.14.0.2/16`.
   - If the line also has a second, longer address after a comma (that's IPv6, a newer kind of
     internet address), you can ignore it. EasyArr only uses the first one.
   - Lost the private key? The same file has it on the `PrivateKey` line.

Your address is the same for every Surfshark server, so you only do this once.

## OpenVPN: get your service credentials

OpenVPN needs a username and password. These are Surfshark **service credentials** — **not** the
email address and password you log in to the website with.

1. Go to **surfshark.com** and log in.
2. Open **VPN → Manual setup → Desktop or mobile → OpenVPN**.
3. Open the **Credentials** tab. If you don't see a username and password yet, click
   **Generate credentials**.
4. Copy the **username** and the **password** (each has a copy icon next to it).

You don't need to download any OpenVPN files. EasyArr already knows Surfshark's servers.

## Fill in EasyArr

1. In the VPN step of the setup (or later in **Settings → VPN**), choose **Surfshark** in the
   **Also works** group.
2. Under **Connection type**, choose **WireGuard** or **OpenVPN** — the same one you prepared
   above.
3. Fill in the fields:

| Connection type | EasyArr field             | What to paste                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| WireGuard       | **WireGuard private key** | The **Private key** from step 6 (ends in `=`)        |
| WireGuard       | **WireGuard address**     | The address from the `Address` line, e.g. `10.14.0.2/16` |
| OpenVPN         | **VPN username**          | The service **username** from the Credentials tab    |
| OpenVPN         | **VPN password**          | The service **password** from the Credentials tab    |

4. **Server country** (optional): pick a country close to you for the best speed, or leave it on
   **Fastest / any**.
5. Press **Connect**. EasyArr tests the connection. You should see **Connected to Surfshark** and
   **Your home IP is hidden**.

There's no port forwarding switch for Surfshark, because Surfshark doesn't offer it. That's
expected.

## If the test fails

- **"The key isn't right" or "Couldn't reach the VPN server" (WireGuard):** you probably copied
  the **Public key** instead of the **Private key**, or missed a character. Copy the private key
  again (44 characters, ending in `=`). Lost it? Make a new key pair (steps 4–8) and use the new
  file.
- **"Username or password was refused" (OpenVPN):** you used your website email and password.
  Use the service credentials from the **Credentials** tab instead. Also check that your
  subscription is still active.
- **"Enter an IPv4 address like …":** the address field only got the long IPv6 part, or the whole
  file. Paste just the part like `10.14.0.2/16` from the `Address` line.
- **"No server matches your choice":** choose **Fastest / any** or another country and press
  **Connect** again.

Back to [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/generic.md -->

# Other providers

_Last checked: 31 October 2026_

EasyArr works with many VPN providers. The most common ones have their own step-by-step guide (see
[VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md)). This page is for all the others:

Windscribe, IVPN, FastestVPN, ExpressVPN, IPVanish, HideMyAss, Privado, PureVPN, TorGuard,
VyprVPN, SlickVPN, Giganews, CyberGhost, VPN Unlimited, VPNSecure, PrivateVPN and Perfect Privacy.

Every provider's website looks different, but the steps are almost always the same.

## Step 1: Find the "manual setup" page

EasyArr isn't an app from your provider, so you need the details for setting up a VPN "by hand".
Log in on your provider's website and look for a page called something like:

- **Manual setup** or **Manual configuration**
- **Router** or **Other devices**
- **Linux**
- **OpenVPN** or **WireGuard** (often under "Downloads" or "Config generator")

If you can't find it, search the provider's help pages for "manual setup" or "OpenVPN". That's also
the best place to check when something below doesn't match what you see.

## Step 2: WireGuard or OpenVPN?

When you pick your provider in EasyArr, it shows which **connection types** it supports. If you can
choose, use **WireGuard** — it's faster and simpler (see [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md)).

## WireGuard: copy three lines from a file

On the manual setup page, generate a **WireGuard configuration** (pick any server — EasyArr only
needs your personal key, and it chooses servers itself). You get a small text file ending in
`.conf`. Open it with any text editor. It looks roughly like this:

```ini
[Interface]
PrivateKey = wOEI9rqqbDwnN8/Bpp22sVz48T71vJ4fYmFWujulwUU=
Address = 10.64.222.21/32
DNS = 10.255.255.1

[Peer]
PublicKey = ...
PresharedKey = ...
Endpoint = ...
```

Copy these values into EasyArr:

| Line in the file | Field in EasyArr        | Notes                                                      |
| ---------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PrivateKey =`   | WireGuard private key   | 44 characters ending in `=`. Keep it secret.               |
| `Address =`      | WireGuard address       | Something like `10.64.222.21/32`. An IPv6 part is ignored. |
| `PresharedKey =` | WireGuard preshared key | Only if EasyArr asks for it and the line exists.           |

Copy only the value after `=` — not the word `PrivateKey` itself. The other lines (DNS, PublicKey,
Endpoint, AllowedIPs) aren't needed: EasyArr already knows your provider's servers.

## OpenVPN: special "service credentials"

Most providers use a **separate username and password for OpenVPN**. They are **not** the email and
password you use on the website. On the manual setup page they're often called "service
credentials", "OpenVPN credentials" or "manual setup credentials". Enter them as **VPN username**
and **VPN password**.

If EasyArr says "Username or password was refused", this mix-up is the most common reason. Also
check that your subscription is active.

### Certificates and keys

A few providers (see the table below) also need a **certificate** and a **key**. You find them in
the OpenVPN file (`.ovpn`) you download from the manual setup page. Open it with a text editor:

- **Client certificate** = everything between `<cert>` and `</cert>`
- **Client key** = everything between `<key>` and `</key>`

Some providers give these as separate files instead (for example `client.crt` and `client.key`).
Then paste the whole content of each file. It's fine to include the `-----BEGIN ...-----` and
`-----END ...-----` lines; EasyArr removes them.

## Hints per provider

"PF" = port forwarding (see [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md#port-forwarding-in-plain-words)). If a hint
doesn't match what you see, your provider's manual setup page is always right.

**Windscribe** — WireGuard or OpenVPN. PF: no.

- WireGuard: private key, address **and** preshared key — all three are required. Use Windscribe's
  WireGuard config generator.
- OpenVPN: the username and password shown by Windscribe's OpenVPN config generator, not your login.
- "Build a Plan" subscription: choose one of the locations you paid for as the server location.
  "Fastest / any" may pick one your plan doesn't include.

**IVPN** — WireGuard or OpenVPN. PF: no.

- WireGuard: private key + address.
- OpenVPN: enter your **account ID** (`i-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`) as username and leave the password empty.
  Your email + password also work.

**FastestVPN** — WireGuard or OpenVPN. PF: no.

- WireGuard: private key + address. You have to ask FastestVPN's support for the WireGuard file.
- OpenVPN: username + password.

**PrivateVPN** — OpenVPN. PF: **yes, automatic**.

- Your PrivateVPN account login and password — **not** the "Proxy login" in the control panel.

**Perfect Privacy** — OpenVPN. PF: **yes, automatic**.

- Username + password.
- If the VPN connects but nothing works, turn off the "TrackStop" filter for fraud in your account.

**CyberGhost** and **VPN Unlimited** — OpenVPN. PF: no.

- Username + password **plus** a client certificate and a client key, all from the provider's
  manual (OpenVPN) setup. See [Certificates and keys](#certificates-and-keys).

**VPNSecure** — OpenVPN. PF: no.

- No username. You need three things instead:
  - **Client certificate** — usually in the file `yourusername.crt`,
  - **Encrypted client key** — usually in the file `yourusername.key`,
  - **Key passphrase** — your VPNSecure account password.

**ExpressVPN, IPVanish, HideMyAss, Privado, PureVPN, TorGuard, VyprVPN, Giganews, SlickVPN** —
OpenVPN. PF: no.

- Username + password. Check the provider's manual setup page to see whether it uses special
  OpenVPN credentials or your normal login.

## Your provider has WireGuard, but EasyArr only offers OpenVPN?

EasyArr can only use WireGuard with a provider when the VPN software inside EasyArr (Gluetun)
supports it. For some providers — for example PureVPN, TorGuard, CyberGhost, VyprVPN, PrivateVPN and
VPN Unlimited — you can still use a WireGuard file through
[Custom: use a config file](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/custom.md). The downside: you then use one fixed server, and automatic
port forwarding isn't available (for PrivateVPN it only works over OpenVPN anyway).

## Step 3: Connect and check

Pick a server location (or "Fastest / any"), turn on port forwarding if your provider has it and
you use torrents, then press **Connect**. EasyArr tests the connection and shows whether your home
IP is hidden. If something goes wrong, EasyArr says what it thinks the problem is — most of the time
it's a credential copied from the wrong place.

Your provider not listed at all? Use [Custom: use a config file](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/custom.md).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/custom.md -->

# Custom: use a config file

_Last checked: 31 October 2026_

Your VPN provider isn't in EasyArr's list? Almost every provider lets you download a **config file**
for "manual setup". EasyArr can use that file directly. Choose **Other / config file** (under
"Custom") in the provider list.

This also works if you run your own VPN server, or if your provider is in the list but EasyArr
only offers OpenVPN for it and you'd rather use WireGuard (see [Other providers](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/generic.md)).

## Before you start

- Log in on your provider's website and find the **manual setup** page (sometimes called "Router",
  "Linux", "Other devices", "OpenVPN" or "WireGuard").
- Download **one** config file. Prefer **WireGuard** (`.conf`) if offered: it's faster and simpler
  (see [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md)). Otherwise take **OpenVPN** (`.ovpn`).
- A config file connects to **one server**. If you want another country, download the file for
  that server and save it in EasyArr again.

## WireGuard (.conf)

Paste the whole file into **WireGuard file (.conf)**, or press **Choose a file instead** and pick
it. Then press **Connect**.

The file must contain these lines. EasyArr checks them when you save:

| Section       | Line           | What it is                         |
| ------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `[Interface]` | `PrivateKey`   | Your personal key (keep it secret) |
| `[Interface]` | `Address`      | Your address inside the VPN        |
| `[Peer]`      | `PublicKey`    | The server's key                   |
| `[Peer]`      | `Endpoint`     | The server's address and port      |
| `[Peer]`      | `PresharedKey` | Optional — used if it's there      |

Good to know:

- **IPv6 is ignored.** EasyArr's VPN uses IPv4 only. If `Address` lists an IPv4 and an IPv6
  address, only the IPv4 one is used. If the file has no IPv4 address at all, it won't work.
- **Only the first `[Peer]` is used.** Lines like `DNS`, `AllowedIPs` or `MTU` are ignored —
  EasyArr sends all download traffic through the VPN anyway.
- **Server names are looked up once.** If `Endpoint` is a name (like `nl1.example.com:51820`)
  rather than numbers, EasyArr looks up its IP address **once, when you save**. If the provider
  later moves that server to a new IP address, the VPN stops connecting (the kill switch keeps you
  safe — downloads just stop). Fix: open **Settings → VPN** and save again.
- If EasyArr says "The server name in your file couldn't be found", check your Umbrel's internet
  connection, or download a file that has an IP address in `Endpoint`.

## OpenVPN (.ovpn)

Paste the whole file into **OpenVPN file (.ovpn)**, or press **Choose a file instead** and pick
it.

If your provider needs a login for OpenVPN (the file then usually contains a line
`auth-user-pass`), also fill in **VPN username** and **VPN password**. Many providers use special
"service credentials" for this, not your website login — check the manual setup page. If your
provider needs no login, leave both empty.

Then press **Connect**.

### Limits of OpenVPN files

The VPN software inside EasyArr (Gluetun) reads your file and changes a few things. Most files work
as they are, but check these points if the connection fails:

- **Server names are looked up once, when you save.** Gluetun needs an IP address in the `remote`
  line, because the kill switch blocks name lookups before the VPN is up. If your file has a name
  (like `remote nl1.example.com 1194`), EasyArr replaces it with that server's current IP address
  when you press Connect. If the provider later moves the server, press Connect again (or download a
  file "with IP addresses", if your provider offers one).
- **Only the first `remote` line is used.** Files with a list of backup servers just use the first
  one.
- **Everything must be inside the one file.** EasyArr only stores this one file. Lines that point
  to other files — like `ca ca.crt`, `cert client.crt` or `auth-user-pass login.txt` — won't work.
  Most providers offer "all-in-one" (inline) files, where certificates are inside blocks like
  `<ca>…</ca>`. Use those. Usernames and passwords go into EasyArr's fields, not into a file.
- **Some options are replaced.** Gluetun sets its own values for things like the login handling
  (`auth-user-pass`), the network device (`dev`) and logging (`verb`). You don't need to change
  anything for this.
