- **No scripts.** Lines starting with `up` or `down` point to script files that don't exist on
  your Umbrel, so the connection fails. Delete those lines, or download the provider's file for
  "router" or "other devices", which usually has none.

## Port forwarding

Automatic port forwarding (where EasyArr asks the provider for a port) isn't possible with a config
file. What works: a **fixed port** your provider gave you — for example one you reserved in your
account, or one that comes with a static IP address.

1. Turn on **Port forwarding**.
2. Enter the port in **Your reserved port** (1024–65535).
3. Press **Connect**.

EasyArr lets incoming connections on that port through the VPN and sets it in qBittorrent for you.
No fixed port? Leave port forwarding off. Torrents still work, just slower — and Usenet doesn't need
it at all (see [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md#port-forwarding-in-plain-words)).

## Where your file is stored

Your config file contains secrets (keys, sometimes passwords). EasyArr stores it **only on your
Umbrel**, in files only EasyArr can read. It's never sent anywhere else and never shown again in
the browser. To change it, paste or choose a new file and save. If you switch to a provider from
the list, the old OpenVPN file is deleted.

## Still not connecting?

- Download a fresh file from your provider — files can expire, and keys can be revoked.
- Try a different server's file.
- Check that your subscription is active.
- Open **Technical details** under the error message. It usually names the line or setting that
  failed.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/family-accounts.md -->

# Family accounts

The account you create in the setup is **your** account. It's the admin account for:

- **Jellyfin**, where you watch movies, shows and music;
- **Jellyseerr**, the request page (it signs you in with your Jellyfin account).

The other apps inside EasyArr don't have logins of their own. Your Umbrel login protects them.

Everyone in your home can get their own Jellyfin account. Then everybody has their own "continue
watching" list, and you choose what each person may watch and request.

> **What you'll need**
>
> - EasyArr set up and finished (the setup's last step is done).
> - About 5 minutes per person.

## 1. Create an account in Jellyfin

1. On the EasyArr home screen, press **Watch** and sign in with your own account.
2. Click your profile picture at the top right, then **Dashboard**.
3. In the menu on the left, click **Users**.
4. Click the **+** button (**Add User**).
5. Type a **Name** and a **Password** for the new person.
6. Under **Library Access**, leave **Enable access to all libraries** ticked, or untick it and
   choose the libraries this person may see (for example only **Movies**).
7. Click **Save**.

The new person can now sign in to Jellyfin with that name and password, on the TV, phone or in the
browser.

### Limit what children can watch (optional)

1. In **Dashboard → Users**, click the person.
2. Open the **Parental Control** tab.
3. Choose a **Maximum allowed parental rating**, for example the rating for 12-year-olds in your
   country.
4. Click **Save**.

Movies and shows above that rating are hidden for this person. It works best when your library has
ratings, which Jellyfin adds by itself for most movies and shows.

## 2. Let them request movies and shows

Everyone with a Jellyfin account can sign in to the request page and ask for movies and shows
right away. Your own requests start downloading at once. Requests from other people wait until you
approve them: you see them under **Requests**, with **Approve** and **Decline** buttons. If you
trust someone, give them **Auto-Approve** (below) and their requests start at once too.

To see or change what someone may do:

1. On the EasyArr home screen, press **Request** and sign in with your own account.
2. Click **Users** in the menu on the left. People appear here after they sign in for the first
   time. To add everyone at once, click **Import Jellyfin Users**.
3. Click **Edit** next to a person.
4. Under **Permissions**, choose what they may do. The most useful ones:
   - **Request**: may ask for movies and shows.
   - **Auto-Approve**: their requests start downloading without your OK.
5. Click **Save Changes**.

To change the starting permissions for everyone who signs in later, go to **Settings → Users →
Default Permissions** on the request page.

## Change a password

- **Your own password:** in Jellyfin, click your profile picture → **Profile**, and change it under
  **Password**. Changing it from EasyArr's Settings comes in a later version.
- **Someone else's password:** in Jellyfin, go to **Dashboard → Users**, click the person, open the
  **Password** tab, type a **New password** and click **Save Password**.

The request page always uses the Jellyfin password, so you only change it in one place.

## Remove an account

In Jellyfin, go to **Dashboard → Users**, click the **⋯** menu next to the person and choose
**Delete**. Their requests on the request page stay until you delete them there too (**Users →
Delete User**).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/remote-access-tailscale.md -->

# Watch away from home (Tailscale)

At home, your TV and phone reach EasyArr's Jellyfin through your home network. Away from home they
can't, because your Umbrel isn't on the internet. That's good: it keeps strangers out.

**Tailscale** is a free app that connects your own devices to each other, wherever they are, as if
they were at home. Nobody else can reach your Umbrel through it. There's an official Tailscale app
for Umbrel.

> **What you'll need**
>
> - A free Tailscale account (sign in with Google, Microsoft, Apple or GitHub).
> - The phone, tablet or laptop you want to watch on.
> - About 10 minutes.

Tailscale and EasyArr's VPN don't get in each other's way. EasyArr's VPN only carries the
downloads. Tailscale only connects your own devices.

## 1. Install Tailscale on your Umbrel

1. Open your Umbrel's **App Store** and search for **Tailscale**.
2. Click **Install**.
3. Open the **Tailscale** app from your Umbrel's home screen.
4. Click **Log in** and sign in to your Tailscale account (or create one).

Your Umbrel is now part of your own private Tailscale network.

## 2. Install Tailscale on your phone or laptop

1. Install **Tailscale** from your device's app store (iPhone, Android) or from
   [tailscale.com/download](https://tailscale.com/download) (Windows, Mac, Linux).
2. Open it and sign in with **the same account** as on the Umbrel.
3. Turn Tailscale on.

## 3. Find your Umbrel's Tailscale address

1. In the Tailscale app on your phone or laptop, open the list of devices.
2. Find your Umbrel. It's usually called **umbrel**.
3. Note its address. It starts with `100.`, for example `100.101.102.103`.

## 4. Watch

Make sure Tailscale is turned on, then use the Tailscale address instead of `umbrel.local`:

| What | Address |
| ---- | ------- |
| Jellyfin (watch) | `http://100.101.102.103:39096` |
| Request page | `http://100.101.102.103:39055` |
| Your Umbrel and the EasyArr dashboard | `http://100.101.102.103` |

Use your own Tailscale address, not the example.

In the **Jellyfin app** on your phone, add the Tailscale address as a second server, or change the
server address to it. The Tailscale address also works at home while Tailscale is on, so you can
simply use it everywhere.

If your Tailscale has **MagicDNS** turned on (the default for new accounts), `http://umbrel:39096`
works too.

## Good to know

- **Speed.** Away from home, video comes from your home internet's **upload** speed, which is often
  much slower than your download speed. If videos stutter, choose a lower quality in the Jellyfin
  app (the ⚙ button while a video plays).
- **TVs** usually can't run Tailscale. At a friend's house, use your phone or laptop instead.
- **Don't open ports on your router** for Jellyfin or EasyArr. Tailscale is the safe way in.
- **Family members** away from home need Tailscale too. You can share your Umbrel with them from
  the Tailscale website (**Share** next to the device), so they don't need access to your other
  devices.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/backup-restore.md -->

# Backups: keep your setup safe

An EasyArr backup holds **your setup, not your movies**. If your Umbrel breaks, or you reinstall
EasyArr, a backup brings everything back in a few minutes: your answers from the setup, your
account, your VPN, the connections between the apps, and what Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr
and Jellyfin remember.

## What's in a backup

| Comes back exactly as it was | Set up again from your answers | Never in a backup |
|---|---|---|
| Your answers, account and VPN settings | qBittorrent | Your movies, shows and music |
| Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr: your shows, movies and artists, history, settings | SABnzbd | Downloads that aren't finished |
| Prowlarr: your search sites | Bazarr | |
| Jellyfin: users, what you watched, libraries, settings | Jellyseerr (past requests are not kept) | |
| | Cleanuparr, Recyclarr, Unpackerr | |

"Set up again" means EasyArr connects those apps the same way the setup did. Changes you made by
hand inside them are not kept.

Your media files stay in **Files → Home → EasyArr → media** on your Umbrel. They are not touched by a
backup or a restore. To keep a copy of them, copy that folder to another drive.

## Download a backup

![Settings → Backups: download a backup, automatic backups and the list of saved backups](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/settings-backups.jpg)

1. Open EasyArr → **Settings** → **Backups**.
2. Leave **Protect with a password** on and pick a password. Write it down somewhere safe:
   without it, the backup can't be opened, not even by EasyArr.
3. Press **Download backup**. It takes about a minute: each app makes its own backup first.
4. Keep the file (it ends in `.easyarr`) somewhere other than your Umbrel, for example on your
   computer or a USB stick.

Why a password? The backup contains your VPN key and your passwords. With a password, the file is
encrypted (AES-256), so anyone who finds it can't read them.

## Automatic backups

EasyArr makes a backup every day at 04:00 (your time) and keeps the newest 7. You can change the
time and how many to keep in **Settings → Backups**, or turn them off.

Automatic backups stay on your Umbrel, without a password, in **Files → Home → EasyArr → backups**. That
protects you from mistakes and broken apps, but not from a broken Umbrel. To keep a copy somewhere
else:

1. Open **Files** on your Umbrel → **EasyArr** → **backups**.
2. Select the newest file → **Download**.
3. Store it somewhere other than your Umbrel.

Or download a password-protected backup from **Settings → Backups** (above).

## Restore a backup

You can restore at any time: from the first setup screen (**Restore from backup**) after a fresh
install, or later from **Settings → Backups**.

1. Press **Restore from backup** and choose your `.easyarr` file. (An automatic backup: press
   **Restore** next to it in **Settings → Backups**.)
2. If the backup has a password, enter it.
3. EasyArr shows what's in the backup. Check it, then press **Restore this backup**.
4. Keep the page open. You'll see each step: the apps restart while their data comes back, then
   EasyArr tests the VPN and connects all apps again. This takes a few minutes.
5. When it says **Your setup is back**, you're done.

Restoring replaces EasyArr's current settings with the ones in the backup.

### If something didn't work

- **"That password doesn't open this backup"**: check the password (upper and lower case count).
- **"This backup file is damaged"**: the file was cut off or changed, for example by an
  incomplete download. Try another copy.
- **"Made by a newer version of EasyArr"**: update EasyArr in the Umbrel App Store first.
- **An app couldn't take its own backup**: EasyArr set it up again from your answers instead.
  It works, but its history from the backup is missing.
- **The VPN didn't connect**: open **Settings → VPN** and test it. Your VPN account may have
  changed since the backup was made.
- **Some connections need attention**: open **Settings → Advanced** → **Repair connections**.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/two-jellyfins.md -->

# Two Jellyfins on one Umbrel

EasyArr brings its own Jellyfin (port **39096**). If the **Jellyfin app from the Umbrel App Store**
is installed too, you have two separate media servers:

- each has its own users, libraries and watch history;
- EasyArr's downloads only show up in **EasyArr's** Jellyfin;
- both use the processor and the disk, which slows things down when they scan or play.

## What to do

Most people only need one. If you don't use the other Jellyfin for anything else:

1. Open the Umbrel App Store → **Jellyfin** → **Uninstall**.
2. On your TV, phone or tablet, connect the Jellyfin app to `http://umbrel.local:39096`
   (EasyArr's Jellyfin) and sign in with your EasyArr account.

If you want to keep both, that's fine too. EasyArr keeps working. Just remember which one has
which movies, and use port **39096** for the ones EasyArr downloads.

The warning on the EasyArr home screen goes away a few minutes after the other app is uninstalled.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

The most common problems and how to fix them, all from the EasyArr dashboard. Can't find yours?
Use **Get help with AI** (see [Getting help](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/getting-help.md)).

## Setup

### The VPN doesn't connect

EasyArr shows what went wrong under **Connect** in the VPN step (or **Settings** → **VPN**). The
most common messages:

- **The key isn't right** or **Username or password was refused**: copy the key or login again
  from your VPN provider's website. For most providers this is *not* your normal account password
  but a separate VPN login. The [VPN guide](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md) for your provider shows where to find it.
- **No server matches your choice**: pick another country, or turn off **Port forwarding** or
  **Free plan** if you don't need them.
- **Couldn't reach the VPN server**: try again in a few minutes, or pick another country.
- **Your home IP is NOT hidden**: don't use EasyArr for downloads until this is fixed. Check the
  settings against the guide and connect again.

While the VPN is down, downloads stop. That's on purpose: the kill switch makes sure nothing goes
out without the VPN.

### Connecting the apps (Finish step) didn't work

1. Wait two minutes and press **Try again**. Right after an install or update, some apps need a moment
   before they answer.
2. If the same line keeps failing, press **Get help with AI** next to it.
3. If you need to, press **Finish anyway**. You can repair the connections later in
   **Settings** → **Advanced** → **Repair connections**.

## On the home screen

### "Not answering: …"

An app isn't responding. Most of the time it's still starting (right after an update or a restart
of your Umbrel, this can take a few minutes).

1. Wait five minutes.
2. Still there? Restart EasyArr: on your Umbrel's home screen, right-click (or long-press) the
   EasyArr icon → **Restart**.
3. Still there after a restart? Use **Get help with AI**.

### "Some connections didn't work"

Press **Repair connections**. It runs the setup's connection step again and explains what's wrong.
Repairing never changes settings you made yourself in the apps.

### "Search sites can't be reached"

Your search sites (indexers) aren't answering through the VPN. Often it's the site itself, or the
VPN server is blocked by that site.

1. Wait 15 minutes: EasyArr tries the sites again by itself.
2. If it stays: pick another VPN country in **Settings** → **VPN**.
3. Some sites block VPNs or bots. Add another site in Prowlarr (see [Search sites](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/indexers.md)).

### "Storage is almost full"

Your Umbrel's disk has less than 10 % free. Delete movies or shows you've watched (in Jellyfin, or
in Sonarr/Radarr with **Delete files**), or move them to another drive.

## Downloads

### A request never starts downloading

Look at **Needs your attention** on the home screen. EasyArr explains there why something hasn't
arrived:

- **Nothing found yet**: your search sites don't have it (yet). EasyArr keeps searching by itself;
  **Search now** searches right away. Adding more search sites helps most.
- **Only in another language or a lower quality**: press the button (for example **Download that
  version**) to take it anyway.
- **A download is stuck**: press **Try another version**. EasyArr removes it and looks for another
  one.

### A torrent is stuck on "Downloading metadata"

Nobody shares this torrent at the moment. EasyArr removes torrents that are stuck for too long by
itself and searches for another one, usually within 15–30 minutes.

### Torrents download slowly

1. Check how many people share the file: in **Advanced** mode, open **qBittorrent** and look at
   **Seeds**. Few seeds means slow, whatever you do.
2. Use a VPN with **port forwarding** if you can. It lets other people connect to you, which often
   makes torrents much faster. See [Port forwarding](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md#port-forwarding-in-plain-words).
3. Try another VPN country in **Settings** → **VPN**. A server close to you is usually faster.

### Usenet downloads fail

Check your Usenet provider in **Settings** → **Usenet** and press **Test this provider**. "Server requires
username and password" means the login is wrong. "Timed out" usually means the server name or port
is wrong. See [Usenet explained](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md).

## Watching

### I can't sign in to Jellyfin or Jellyseerr

Use the username and password you chose in the setup's **Account** step. Family members get their
own accounts, see [Family accounts](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/family-accounts.md).

### My TV or phone can't find the Jellyfin server

Some devices don't understand `umbrel.local`. Use your Umbrel's IP address instead, for example
`http://192.168.1.20:39096`. Your router's list of connected devices shows the IP address.

Away from home, Jellyfin only works through Tailscale, see
[Remote access with Tailscale](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/remote-access-tailscale.md).

### Videos stop and buffer

Your Umbrel may have to convert the video while it plays (**transcoding**), which needs a lot of
power without a graphics chip, see [System requirements](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/system-requirements.md#graphics-gpu).

1. In the Jellyfin app, choose a lower quality while the video plays (the ⚙ button).
2. Pick the **Save space** quality in **Settings** → **Libraries & quality**, so future downloads
   are smaller and play directly on more devices.

### There are two Jellyfins

If the official Umbrel Jellyfin app is installed too, you have two separate libraries. See
[Two Jellyfins](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/two-jellyfins.md).

## Backups

### A restore asks for a password

The backup was made with **Protect with a password** on. Without that password the file can't be
opened. See [Backups](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/backup-restore.md).

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/faq.md -->

# Frequently asked questions

## About EasyArr

### What is EasyArr?

An app for your Umbrel that turns it into your own streaming service. You ask for a movie, a show
or an album, and EasyArr finds it, downloads it through a VPN, sorts it and makes it ready to watch
in Jellyfin. It installs and connects about a dozen well-known media apps for you. See
[How EasyArr works](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md).

### Does it cost anything?

EasyArr is free and open source. You may need to pay for other things:

- a **VPN** (a few euros or dollars a month),
- for **Usenet** only: a Usenet provider and usually an indexer.

Torrents themselves cost nothing.

### Is it legal?

EasyArr is a tool, like a web browser. The apps inside it are legal, open-source software used by
millions of people. What you download with it is your responsibility: only download content you
have the right to download and share, and follow the laws where you live.

### Who makes EasyArr? Is it from Umbrel?

EasyArr is an independent open-source project by w1kyu. It isn't made, checked or endorsed by
Umbrel. The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr).

### Does EasyArr send my data anywhere?

No. Your settings, passwords and keys stay on your Umbrel. EasyArr and the apps inside only go
online to:

- search and download (always through your VPN),
- fetch posters, descriptions and subtitles for your library (for example from TheMovieDB),
- check for updates (EasyArr reads the newest version number from its GitHub store).

Nothing is collected about you. EasyArr also switches off the anonymous usage statistics that
Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr and Bazarr would otherwise send to their developers. **Get help with AI** never sends anything
by itself: you see the text and copy it yourself, see [Getting help](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/getting-help.md).

## Setting up

### Do I really need a VPN?

For downloading, yes. EasyArr won't download without one. With torrents, everyone who shares a file
can see the internet address of everyone else who shares it. A VPN hides yours. See
[VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md).

You can finish the setup without a VPN and add one later in **Settings → VPN**. Watching what you
already have keeps working, but nothing new downloads until the VPN is connected.

### Which VPN should I use?

Any provider in the list works. For torrents, the **Best for torrents** group is best because those
providers offer **port forwarding**, which makes torrents faster. The [VPN basics](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/vpn/README.md)
page compares them, and every provider has a step-by-step guide.

### Torrents or Usenet?

Not sure? Start with torrents: free and nothing else to sign up for. Usenet is faster and more
reliable but costs money. You can switch, or use both, later in **Settings → Download method**. See
[Torrents 101](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/torrents-101.md) and [Usenet 101](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/usenet-101.md).

### Which search sites should I add?

EasyArr doesn't pick or recommend any. [Search sites](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/indexers.md) explains how to find and add
some in Prowlarr.

### My Umbrel only has 4 GB of memory. Will it work?

It will run, but slowly, and other Umbrel apps may become slow too. See
[System requirements](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/system-requirements.md).

## Everyday use

### Where are my movies and shows?

In **Files → Home → EasyArr → media** on your Umbrel. Jellyfin shows everything in there. See
[Where your files are](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#where-your-files-are).

### Can I use an external drive or a NAS?

Not yet. EasyArr stores everything on your Umbrel's main disk for now.

### How do I request music?

The request page only knows movies and shows. Music is added in **Lidarr**: on the EasyArr home
screen, switch to **Advanced**, open **Lidarr**, then **Add New** and search for an artist. EasyArr
already set Lidarr up, so the album downloads and appears in Jellyfin under **Music**.

### Can my family use it?

Yes. Everyone gets their own Jellyfin account, with their own watch history and the libraries you
choose. See [Family accounts](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/family-accounts.md).

### Can I watch when I'm not at home?

Yes, with the free Tailscale app. See [Remote access with Tailscale](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/remote-access-tailscale.md).

### Can I use Plex instead of Jellyfin?

No. EasyArr is built around Jellyfin, which is free and open source. Jellyfin has apps for most
TVs, phones and streaming sticks.

### I already have the Jellyfin app from the Umbrel App Store. What now?

Then you have two separate Jellyfins. See [Two Jellyfins](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/two-jellyfins.md).

### Why didn't my request download?

Look at **Needs your attention** on the EasyArr home screen. It explains the most common reasons,
for example that only another language or a lower quality exists, and offers a button to fix it.
See [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#a-request-never-starts-downloading).

## Updates, backups, uninstalling

### How do I update EasyArr?

When there's a new version, the EasyArr home screen tells you. Install it from your Umbrel's
**App Store** (**Updates**). Your settings and media are kept.

### Should I make backups?

Yes. A backup keeps your answers, accounts, VPN settings and each app's history, so you can get
everything back after a broken disk or a new Umbrel. Turn on automatic backups in
**Settings → Backups**. See [Backups](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/backup-restore.md).

### What happens if I uninstall EasyArr?

Umbrel deletes EasyArr's settings and the apps' databases. Your movies, shows and music in
**Files → Home → EasyArr** stay, and so do the automatic backups in its `backups` folder. Delete
that folder yourself if you want the space back. Download a backup first if you might reinstall.

---

<!-- source: https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/getting-help.md -->

# Getting help

Something doesn't work? There are three ways to get help, from fastest to slowest:

1. Look for your problem in [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md).
2. Ask an AI chat (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, …) with **Get help with AI**.
3. Open an issue on GitHub.

## Get help with AI

![The Get help with AI window: a box for your goal, the preview of the text, and the copy buttons](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/docs/images/ai-help.jpg)

EasyArr can write the question for you. It describes your setup, what went wrong and the newest
lines from the apps' logs, so the AI can give an answer that fits your Umbrel.

1. Press **Get help with AI**. You find it:
   - next to every error in the setup wizard,
   - on the Finish step when connecting the apps didn't work,
   - in **Help**, at the top right of every EasyArr page,
   - next to problems on the home screen.
2. Type in a few words under **What I was trying to do**, for example "Download a movie" or
   "Connect the VPN".
3. Read the preview. That is exactly what gets copied, nothing else.
4. Press **Copy**, or one of the chat buttons (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Le Chat): they copy the
   text and open that chat in a new tab.
5. Paste it into the chat (Ctrl+V, or ⌘+V on a Mac) and send it.

The AI may ask you to try something. If it suggests terminal commands, ask it for a way that works
from the EasyArr dashboard: EasyArr is built so you never need a terminal.

### What EasyArr hides before you copy

Before anything leaves EasyArr, these are replaced with `[REDACTED:…]`:

- passwords, API keys, tokens and VPN keys (`[REDACTED:password]`, `[REDACTED:apikey]`,
  `[REDACTED:key]`, `[REDACTED:token]`),
- usernames and e-mail addresses,
- your public IP address (`[REDACTED:ip]`),
- the names of your Usenet servers, VPN servers and search sites (`[REDACTED:host]`).

Addresses inside your home network (like `192.168.1.20`) stay visible, because they often help to
find a problem and don't identify you on the internet. Tick **Also hide addresses in my home
network** if you want them hidden too.

If EasyArr ever finds one of your passwords or keys still in the text, it refuses to show the
preview instead of risking it. Please [report that](#open-an-issue-on-github).

## Download diagnostics

The diagnostics file is a `.zip` with the same information in more detail. It's useful for a
GitHub issue or for someone who helps you.

1. Open **Help** (top right) and press **Download diagnostics** (also in the **Get help with AI** window).
2. The file is called something like `easyarr-diagnostics-2026-11-15-1030.zip`.

Inside are:

| File | What it says |
|---|---|
| `diagnostics.json` | EasyArr version, hardware, your setup choices, which apps answer, the VPN's state (no IP addresses) |
| `ai-prompt.txt` | The same text as **Get help with AI** |
| `logs/` | The newest lines from EasyArr, the VPN and each app's log |
| `README.txt` | What the file is and what was hidden |

The same things are hidden as in the AI prompt. It's still a good idea to open the zip and have a
look before you share it.

## Open an issue on GitHub

If neither the docs nor an AI could help, or you think you found a bug:

1. Go to [github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/issues](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/issues) and press
   **New issue**. You need a free GitHub account.
2. Pick **Bug report**, **Feature request** or **VPN guide is outdated**.
3. Fill in the form. For a bug, attach the diagnostics zip or paste the AI prompt from the preview.

Never paste a password or key into an issue: issues are public. If you did by accident, change
that password right away.

Found a security problem? Don't open a public issue. See
[SECURITY.md](https://github.com/w1kyu/easyarr/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for how to report it
privately.
